result_text:
`analyzeLandscape` is now an alias of `updateLandscape` in the CLI, with the same options and behaviour. I compiled the `cli` module offline and it passed. I could not run the CLI to check the help output or an end-to-end landscape run, because the sandbox asked for approval to run `java`. Those checks are still open.

What changed:

- **`cli/.../Commands.java`**: added `ANALYZE_LANDSCAPE = "analyzeLandscape"` and its description, which says it is the landscape counterpart of the analysis commands and the same as `updateLandscape`. It is listed in the no-argument usage overview, with the landscape options. `updateLandscape` stays in the list.
- **`cli/.../CommandLineInterface.java`**: `run()` dispatches both names to the same `updateLandscape(args)` method. In that method, `-help` prints the name the user typed (`args[0]`) and picks the matching description, so `updateLandscape -help` keeps its own usage.
- **`README.md`**: the README had no command reference, so I added a short "Landscape report" section covering `analyzeLandscape -analysisRoot <folder>`, the output paths, and that `updateLandscape` is kept for existing scripts.

I did not touch `CLAUDE.md`, which still lists `updateLandscape` among the main commands. Nothing is committed.
